documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM
INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported record physical performance for FY26, achieving its highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity. The company recorded a gross refining margin (GRM) of $9.2 per barrel for the full year and $13.75 per barrel for Q4 FY26. CPCL is executing a Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project of INR 1,600 crores and a retail outlet project of INR 400 crores. Additionally, the Board recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, bringing the total dividend for the year to a record INR 62 per share. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for FY25, representing 99.5% of its installed capacity.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects its operational and financial momentum to continue into the new financial year.
guidance.quote: To summarize, we continue to deliver resilient operational and financial performance and see the momentum to continue in the new financial year as well.

guidance.claim: The company expects to see a lot of commissioning of retail outlets in the financial year 2026-27.
guidance.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

guidance.claim: CPCL has a scheduled maintenance and inspection of one of its refinery units close to September or October.
guidance.quote: But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.

guidance.claim: The company may ramp up Hexane production in the coming year.
guidance.quote: And if you talk about Hexane, I have doubled my capacity. So again, in the coming year, I may ramp up this production.

guidance.claim: The company expects a higher throughput in FY26 compared to the previous year on the operational side.
guidance.quote: So, you can expect a throughput which is higher than last year on the operational part.

guidance.claim: The company expects normal maintenance CAPEX to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores for the next two years.
guidance.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL stepped up LPG production to meet national requirements amid global supply uncertainties.
demand_outlook.quote: With global uncertainties affecting the availability of LPG all over the world, CPCL is happy to step up the requirement when the nation needed it.

demand_outlook.claim: Cracks in recent months have remained reasonable and close to long-term averages.
demand_outlook.quote: But still in these months, the cracks are reasonable enough and close to our long-term averages.

demand_outlook.claim: The company expects to sustain long-term average gross refining margins over a monthly period.
demand_outlook.quote: When I look for a month average kind of a period, I feel I'll be able to sustain the long-term averages.

demand_outlook.claim: There is a clear shortfall of MS in the southern market, with production being less than demand.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market is mostly aligned with national growth projections.
demand_outlook.quote: As far as others are concerned, we have seen the southern market to be mostly aligned to the national growth projection.

demand_outlook.claim: The company sees a 3% growth forecast for HSD, compared to around 2.5% in the southern region.
demand_outlook.quote: HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL's capex for the current year was INR 856 crores compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: Project execution has started for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project is valued at INR 1,600 crores, while the retail outlet project is INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The INR 2,000 crores capex for LOBS and retail projects will be spent over two to three years, alongside a normal annual capex of INR 500 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years. Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: The new LOBS unit will add 250 KTPA of Group 2 and Group 3 capacity.
capex_expansion.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the CBR project is Rs. 36,354 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery has an approximate capital cost of Rs. 36,000 Crore and a 9 million metric ton capacity.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

capex_expansion.claim: The company expects to add another Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores per year for the LOBS project.
capex_expansion.quote: And with this project, another Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores you can add for each of the year.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL achieved a gross refining margin of $9.2 per barrel for the financial year 2025-26.
margins_costs.quote: The gross refining margin, GRM, for financial year 2025- '26 was $9.2 per barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for the fourth quarter was $13.75 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core gross refining margin for the quarter was $10.3 per barrel.
Forex losses were approximately INR 200 crores for the quarter and INR 350 crores for the full year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: Niche products contribute around 15% of CPCL's margins.
margins_costs.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7%–8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins.

margins_costs.claim: The full-year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: The company's Q4 GRM was $6.22 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: In absolute rupee terms, the quarterly inventory gain was Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: On an annual basis, the inventory resulted in a loss of $0.06 per barrel or Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for 9M 2024-25 was reported at 3.75 $/BBl.
The operating expenditure (net) was 945 Crore for 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput in the fourth quarter reached 2.93 MMT, representing 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved its best fuel and loss of 7.73%, best MBN of 69.8%, and best EII of 84% in FY25-26.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved the best fuel and loss of 7.73%, best MBN of 69.8% and best EII of 84% in the current financial year '25-'26, surpassing our previous best records achieved in the last financial year, this was driven by the effective implementation of energy conservation initiatives and significantly improved operational reliability.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved record production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel and 1.318 MMT for petrol.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved its highest-ever distillate yield of 79.1%.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: LPG production reached a record 447 TMT during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: The company has three crude units.
One of the crude units went for a maintenance shutdown in 2024-25.
orders_capacity.quote: In 2024-25, we had a maintenance shutdown of one of our crude units.

orders_capacity.claim: The Manali Refinery has an installed capacity of 10.5 MMTPA.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.18 at a gross level.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings are INR 1,900 crores, while net borrowings are INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: The net debt ratio is 0.09, which is less than 0.1.
capital_allocation.quote: If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, bringing the total dividend for the year to INR 62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-equity ratio as of March 31, 2025, was 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Absolute debt stood at Rs. 3,100 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: Net worth was Rs. 7,939 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: The company is working with a 2:1 debt-equity ratio for the JV.
capital_allocation.quote: Presently, we are working with a 2:1 debt equity for this JV.

risks_headwinds.claim: Logistical constraints and volatile crude oil prices present challenges for the company.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Significant rupee movement during the quarter and year impacted other expenses.
risks_headwinds.quote: As we talk because the rupee movement is significant during the quarter as well as year, that is what is accounting significantly.

risks_headwinds.claim: Around 30% to 40% of Middle East cargo flows were temporarily disturbed.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: The primary reason for the decline in profits was international cracks.
risks_headwinds.quote: The primary reason is the international cracks.

risks_headwinds.claim: Provision for contingent liabilities was 9 Crore for 9M 2024-25.
CST Under recovery was 246 Crore for 9M 2024-25.
